messages.author: 20eabdeae3d6d452
messages.subject: nondiag_mass option in RStan 2.5?
parts:
Hi Stan Users,

I upgraded to RStan 2.5, but it seems that the "nondiag_mass" option has disappeared:

fit <- stan(model_code=model_code, data=schools_dat,
            iter=1000, chains=4, nondiag_mass=TRUE)

Warning messages:
1: In is_arg_recognizable(dot_arg_names, c("chain_id", "init_r", "test_grad",  :
  nondiag_mass not found.
2: In is_arg_recognizable(names(dots), c("chain_id", "init_r", "test_grad",  :
  nondiag_mass not found.

This works fine in RStan in 2.4 and previous.  Am I missing a change in syntax?

Thanks,
Eric

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] nondiag_mass option in RStan 2.5?
parts:
The way of configuring the sampling algorithm has been changed since 2.0.
Now it uses an argument called control.

Only after rstan 2.5, warning messages are added for passing unknown arguments.

Jiqiang

On Sat, Jan 03, 2015 at 03:41:52PM -0800, ecb...@northshore.org wrote:
> This explains a lot :-)
>
> I tried:
>
> fit <- stan(model_code=model_code, data=schools_dat,
> iter=1000, chains=4, control=list(nondiag_mass=TRUE))
>
> and this seems to work. Thanks for your reply.

No, that would not work: there is not such an option since the change.
Try the following instead and see the doc please:

fit <- stan(model_code=model_code, data=schools_dat,
iter=1000, chains=4, control = list(metric = "unit_e"))


Besides, the type of sampler is printed out when print is applied to a stanfit object.
